title: Console observability MVP slice: mandatory scope reductions and launch acceptance
creator: Leila Gomez
description:
Goal: Deliver a minimal, production-safe observability surface for Redwood Console that gives engineering and customer-facing teams basic insights into model latency, per-route cost breakdown, and request traces for high-severity errors. This ticket defines the mandatory scope reductions (MVP cuts) agreed by PM, Eng, and Design to meet the April launch window while preserving the core value proposition for early adopters.

Background: Our initial PRD included three distinct pillars: interactive dashboards, full-span distributed tracing, and token-level cost breakdown. Engineering signal showed the tracing integration and token-level provenance would add 3–4 sprints of work given required infra changes (sampling backend, span schema, retention, and storage tiering). To keep the release date and a coherent product, we propose scoped reductions listed below and acceptance criteria for the trimmed MVP.

Key non-goals for MVP (explicit cuts):
- No full distributed out-of-the-box tracing across third-party model backends (deferred). We will provide sampled error traces only for Redwood-hosted inference.
- No token-by-token provenance UI for now — token-level cost will be presented as aggregated per-request tokens and bucketed per-route distributions.
- No long-term raw trace storage beyond 7 days in the product; longer retention delegated to export hooks to customer S3/Kinesis.
- No end-user configurable ingest pipelines (ETL) in initial release.

MVP deliverables (in-scope):
- Dashboards: 3 templated dashboards (Latency Overview, Error Rates & Top Routes, Cost-at-a-Glance) with date range filtering, basic grouping (by model, by route), and CSV export.
- Tracing: sampled request traces for Redwood-hosted requests that exceed a latency or error threshold; trace view with timeline, top-level spans, and link to related request in logs. Sampling rate configurable by admin in the console (default: 1%).
- Cost breakdown: per-route aggregated token usage and cost estimate for the selected time range; ability to attribute cost to model & deployment variant.
- Export hooks: CSV and S3 export for dashboards and trace summaries.

Success metrics (post-launch):
- >50% of active trial accounts use at least one dashboard within the first 30 days.
- Mean time to surface a critical error (from occurrence to viewable trace) < 10 minutes for Redwood-hosted traffic.
- Cost dashboard is used in at least 30% of customers with >$1k monthly spend to identify cost-savings opportunities.
acceptance_criteria: Latency Overview dashboard renders with data for last 24h, 7d, 30d and supports time-range switching with <= 500ms UI latency
Error Rates dashboard surfaces top 10 routes by error rate and allows filtering by model and deployment variant
Cost-at-a-Glance shows aggregated token counts and estimated cost per route for the selected range; values align within 3% of billing table for sample accounts
Trace sampling pipeline captures traces for Redwood-hosted requests that exceed 2x P50 latency or any 5xx error and displays trace timeline with span names and durations
Admin control to set sampling rate (0.1%–10%) is present and persists across sessions
CSV export for current dashboard view downloads within 30s for datasets <= 10k rows
Export-to-S3 setup flow completes with valid credentials and one successful test export
Instrumented e2e smoke test demonstrates a traced error created in staging and visible in console within 10 minutes
decisions: Cut token-by-token provenance UI; instead expose aggregated token counts and route-level attribution (tradeoff: reduces engineering risk and storage cost; cost of less granular debugging retained via exports)
Restrict full distributed tracing to Redwood-hosted backends for MVP; postpone multi-backend trace correlation (reduces schema and ingestion complexity)
Default sampling to 1% with admin override; this balances observability with cost and storage constraints
7-day retention cap for raw traces in product UI; provide export hooks for customers needing longer retention
follow_ups: Phase 2: add token-level provenance and interactive token timeline (dep: quantization cost modeling)
Phase 2: integrate tracing across Dedicated and Private runtimes with OTEL connectors
Post-launch: implement retention tiers and paid retention add-on (billing integration required ENG-4272)
Design: craft microcopy and onboarding tour for dashboards (DES-415)
